status.en: 149 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 38% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 149 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 38 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits have intensified attacks across northern Nigeria, seizing eight communities in Taraba, killing and abducting residents in Kaduna, Kebbi and Plateau, and turning a Benue market into a killing ground. Islamist forces remain active, with the military rejecting any ceasefire and continuing a sustained offensive. Government officials pledged to recover N400 billion in unpaid charges and address power shortages, while political figures accused former administrations of harming industry. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bandittene har økt angrepene i Nord-Nigeria, tatt kontroll over åtte lokalsamfunn i Taraba, drept og bortført innbyggere i Kaduna, Kebbi og Plateau, og gjort et marked i Benue til en drapsplass. Islamistiske styrker er fortsatt aktive, mens militæret avviser enhver våpenhvile og fortsetter en vedvarende offensiv. Regjeringsrepresentanter lovet å inndrive N400 billion i ubetalte krav og å løse strømkrisen, mens politikere anklaget tidligere regjeringer for å skade industrien. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
